# Example page conventions (`example/lib/pages/`)

Each page demonstrates one widget or one concept; split a page rather than cramming a second concept in. Before restyling a page or the scaffold, read `DESIGN.md`.

## Shape

- Name the file in snake_case (`button_basic.dart`) and the class `<Feature>ExamplePage` (`ButtonBasicExamplePage`), the form almost every page class takes.
- Build the page from `ExampleScaffold(title:, description:, gradient:, children:)` and `ExampleSection(title:, description:, child:)` in `example/lib/widgets/example_scaffold.dart`. The scaffold carries the root `WDiv`, the centred `max-w-4xl` column, the gradient header and the section card, so a page does not rebuild them; `gradient` takes a `from-* to-*` pair and defaults to `from-blue-500 to-indigo-600`.
- Interactive demos use a `StatefulWidget` and `setState` with state a reader can drive: a `bool _isLoading` toggle, an `int _counter`, a `Future.delayed` that simulates async work. Use realistic content ("John Doe", "user@example.com"), never lorem ipsum, and show three to five variants per feature.
- A className with three or more concerns is a triple-quoted string with one concern per line, so a reader can scan it.

## State demos

Show the className that fires the state, for example `'bg-blue-500 hover:bg-blue-600 disabled:bg-gray-400'`. For a custom state, drive it with `states: {'selected'}` and the `selected:` prefix.

## What never goes in `example/lib/pages/`

Long explanatory copy, which belongs in `doc/`, and production logic: a page is a pure demo.
